context: The array to sort is nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2]. It contains 6 elements at indices 0 through 5. The goal is to sort them in nondecreasing order.

On each pass, i points to the first element in the unsorted range, and k records the index of the minimum found there. Green marks the unsorted portion, gray cells on the left mark the sorted prefix, and a brace above marks the current unsorted range. After selecting k, swap the minimum nums[k] with the first element nums[i] of the range, extending the sorted prefix one place to the right.
description: Of the eleven frames, the first ten show five passes with a selection frame and a swap frame for each. Selection shows i and k after the scan, omitting individual inner-loop comparisons. The swap frame shows the resulting array with arcs above and below the positions just swapped and hides the i and k labels. The eleventh frame shows that one element remains, so a sixth pass is unnecessary.

frames.explanation: Pass 1 selection: nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2]. After scanning the unsorted index range [0, 5], i = 0 points to the first element, 4, and k = 1 points to the minimum, 1. There are two 1s, at indices 1 and 3. The strict less-than comparison keeps the leftmost at k = 1. There is no sorted prefix yet, and no swap has occurred.

summary: Each pass selects the smallest element in the unsorted range and swaps it with the first element in that range, extending the sorted prefix by one.
title: Selection sort
